item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Construction begins on permanent site for The Wisbech Academy
Work has officially started on the permanent building for The Wisbech Academy on Weasenham Road. While the school had initially hoped to open the new site in 2027, the Brooke Weston Trust has confirmed the move-in date is now scheduled for between Easter and the summer of 2028. Officials state the extra time is necessary to ensure the quality of the new facility.
The academy is currently operating from temporary modular buildings nearby, where it recently expanded to accommodate Year 9 students. The school continues to share some facilities with the neighbouring Thomas Clarkson Academy, and staff say they remain committed to providing high-quality education throughout the construction period.

Further roadworks scheduled for Barton Road in Wisbech
Drivers in Wisbech are being warned of more disruption on Barton Road. Anglian Water is returning to the route, which serves as the main link to Wisbech St Mary, to carry out further improvements. Site preparations begin this Monday, with the main works starting the following week.
The project involves installing a new kiosk and enclosure at the pumping station, followed by the installation of a new sewer pipe in an adjacent field. Anglian Water has acknowledged the frustration caused by previous closures and thanked residents for their patience while these final stages are carried out.

item.title: Inquest concludes into fatal A47 collision near King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Inquest concludes into fatal A47 collision near King’s Lynn
An inquest at Norfolk Coroner’s Court has heard that 26-year-old Nerijus Vysniauskas died after being struck by a heavy goods vehicle on the A47 near Tilney All Saints. The incident occurred on the morning of December 2, 2024.
The coroner concluded that the driver of the vehicle was unaware of the collision and would not have had sufficient time to react. Forensic evidence indicated the pedestrian was likely hit by a protruding part of the lorry. While the driver had previously faced charges regarding the incident, the Crown Prosecution Service later dropped the case. Toxicology reports confirmed the presence of alcohol and stimulants in the victim’s system at the time of his death.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/pedestrian-struck-and-killed-on-a47-was-not-seen-by-lorry-dr-9481564/

item.title: Wisbech friends complete charity skydive in memory of Jake Young
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech friends complete charity skydive in memory of Jake Young
Two friends from Wisbech have raised £450 for the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation after completing a skydive at Sibson Airfield near Peterborough. Angel Cobb and Ewen Dougal took on the challenge this past Saturday to honour their close friend, Jake Young. Mr Young, a former Thomas Clarkson Academy student, passed away last year at the age of 24.
The pair decided to face their fears to support the charity, which funds research into diabetes treatments and a potential cure. Ms Cobb described the experience as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, while Mr Dougal said he found the jump thoroughly enjoyable. The funds raised will support the foundation’s ongoing work to improve the lives of those living with the condition.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Foodbank appeals for harvest donations
King’s Lynn Foodbank is calling on the community to support its work this harvest season. The charity is asking local organisations hosting harvest festivals to donate collected items to help provide emergency food parcels. Between September 2025 and August 2026, the food bank distributed over 5,500 parcels, with nearly a third going to children.
Strategic project manager Helen Gilbert says demand remains high and the charity is seeking donations of canned goods, pasta, rice, and hygiene products. The food bank now operates from the Connections hub on County Court Road, with additional satellite centres in Gaywood and South Lynn. Residents can find a list of required items and local supermarket drop-off points on the King’s Lynn Foodbank website.

Wisbech Lions Club revitalised with seven new members
The Wisbech Lions Club has been saved from closure following the induction of seven new members. The group was sworn in by zone chairman John Potter during a ceremony at St John’s Church in Parson Drove over the weekend. The club had previously faced the prospect of folding as long-standing members approached retirement.
Club president Michelle Whiting says the new team is now preparing to support the community through various local initiatives, including the return of the annual Christmas Santa Sleigh. During the same event, the club presented a one-thousand-pound donation to the Arthur Rank Hospice, which provides palliative care to residents in Wisbech and the surrounding area.

King’s Lynn Corn Exchange to light up for Air Ambulance Week
The King’s Lynn Corn Exchange will be illuminated on Wednesday, September 9, to mark Air Ambulance Week. The landmark building in the Tuesday Market Place is joining other sites across the region to highlight the work of the East Anglian Air Ambulance.
The charity is currently fundraising for a new base in Cambridge, which must relocate before Cambridge Airport closes in 2030. While £3.6 million has been raised so far, a further £4.4 million is required. Residents are encouraged to share photos of the illuminated building on social media to support the campaign. Wisbech man raises over £20,000 for hospice after Kilimanjaro climb
A Wisbech man has successfully reached the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro, raising more than £20,780 for the hospice that cared for his late brother. Simon Chaplin completed the eight-day trek in memory of his brother, Richard, who passed away last December at the age of 49.
Mr. Chaplin aimed to raise £17,991 for St Peter’s Hospice in Bristol, representing one pound for every day of his brother’s life. Despite facing freezing temperatures and difficult conditions during the climb, he reached the 19,341ft summit on August 16. Mr. Chaplin has thanked everyone who supported his fundraising efforts, noting that the experience has given him greater confidence in his own abilities.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Conservation work begins at King’s Lynn’s historic Custom House
Conservation work has officially begun at the Custom House in King’s Lynn to preserve the Grade I listed building for the future. The project aims to restore the historic stonework, windows, and cupola while upgrading the interior to create a flexible, accessible space for the community. Planned improvements include a new platform lift and updated facilities, with further enhancements to the surrounding Purfleet Quay expected by spring 2027.
Originally commissioned in 1683 by Sir John Turner and designed by architect Henry Bell, the building served as a merchants' exchange before becoming a customs house. The council is now seeking old photographs or personal stories from residents to help document the landmark’s rich maritime history.
